LITERATURE IN ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Characterisation - Point of view - Lang, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Characterisation - Point of view - Lang.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Characterisation - Point of view - Lang.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Characterisation - Point of view - Lang.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Characterisation - Point of view - Lang.

2. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. where is the library

3. When practising Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse -, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse -.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse -.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse -.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse -.

4. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. No full stops

5. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. going
   C. went
   D. goed

6. When practising Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla.

7. When practising Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.

8. When practising Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.

9. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only a describing word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

10. When practising Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - , which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .
   B. Use insults to “practise” Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .
   D. Copy random text without understanding Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .

11. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. blue
   C. happiness
   D. quickly

12. When practising Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse - and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

1. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Characterisation - Point of view - Lang.

2. A — Where is the library?

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse -.

4. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

5. C — went

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.

9. D — A person, place, thing, or idea

10. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .

11. A — run

12. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse -; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
